encounters.title: The Fairy Briefing
encounters.description: A Fairy Consortium analyst appears on a secure League intelligence channel, her wings flickering with anxiety rather than their usual holographic flair. 'Commander Dave. I am breaking protocol by contacting you directly. The crystals are not what we believed. Our long-range resonance monitors have detected harmonic instabilities — frequencies that should not exist in stable fuel deposits. Something is waking up inside the crystal lattice.' Dave studies the data scrolling across his tactical display. The numbers do not lie. They never do.

choices.text: "Transmit all resonance data to League Science Division. I want a full spectral analysis within forty-eight hours."

outcome.description: Dave routes the fairy data through three independent analysis teams. The results converge on a single conclusion: the crystal instability is accelerating, and it correlates with increased extraction rates across the multiverse. Someone — everyone — is mining too deep, too fast. Dave files the report under 'Critical' and begins drafting contingency protocols.

choices.text: "Interesting. What does the Consortium want in exchange for exclusive access to this data?"

outcome.description: The fairy hesitates. She expected alarm, not negotiation. Dave watches her recalculate. 'Trade concessions in the Amber Corridor,' she says finally. Dave nods. The data arrives. The concessions cost less than a single patrol cruiser. Information is always the cheapest weapon.

choices.text: "The Consortium profits from instability. Their data may be fabricated to manipulate crystal markets."

outcome.description: The fairy's wings droop. 'You are making a mistake, Commander.' Dave terminates the channel. But he does not delete the data. He stores it on a private server, accessible only to him. Dismissal and disbelief are not the same thing. Dave dismisses publicly and investigates privately.

encounters.title: The Twilight Bazaar
encounters.description: Dave enters the Twilight Bazaar in civilian clothes — a rare concession to operational necessity. The market sprawls across a hollowed-out asteroid, a labyrinth of neon and whispered deals where every faction's spies pretend not to recognise each other. Dave moves through the crowd with rigid efficiency, cataloguing faces, exits, and weapons. A merchant waves him toward a back stall draped in star charts. 'Commander. You look uncomfortable out of uniform. I have something that will make the discomfort worthwhile.'

choices.text: "Show me. And if this is a waste of my time, I will remember your face."

outcome.description: The merchant unfurls a star chart older than any League cartography. The crystal deposits are marked — but so are deeper structures, veins that run beneath the known deposits like roots beneath a forest. 'The crystals are the fruit,' the merchant whispers. 'This shows the tree.' Dave pays without haggling. He rolls the chart carefully and tucks it inside his coat. The tree. He has been fighting over fruit.

choices.text: "That chart is a strategic asset. Under League Security Protocol Seven, I am requisitioning it."

outcome.description: Dave produces his League credentials. The merchant's smile vanishes. The chart changes hands without payment. Dave studies it under the harsh bazaar lights. The deep crystal structures are unmistakable. This is not geology. This is architecture. Something built these veins. The merchant glares at his back. Dave files the expression under 'acceptable consequences.'

choices.text: "I will examine it here. Photograph the relevant sections. Leave no transaction trail."

outcome.description: Dave's scanner captures every detail of the ancient chart without leaving a purchase record. The merchant shrugs — payment or not, the information is loose. Dave reviews the scans aboard the Iron Paw. The deep crystal structures are real. They predate every known civilisation in the multiverse. Something ancient built the crystal network. Dave does not speculate. He gathers more data.

encounters.title: The Lion's Gambit
encounters.description: A Lion Sovereignty envoy arrives at League headquarters with unprecedented ceremony — honour guard, diplomatic flags, a personal letter from the Pride Council sealed in gold wax. The message is extraordinary: the lions propose a military alliance against the growing instability. 'The Pride recognises the League's strength,' the envoy intones. 'Together, we could impose order on the entire crystal network.' Dave reads the letter twice. Three times. The lions have never offered partnership. They have only ever offered subordination dressed in silk.

choices.text: "The League accepts the Pride Council's proposal. We will draft joint operational parameters."

outcome.description: Dave shakes the envoy's paw. The grip is warm, practiced, and utterly insincere on both sides. Within days, Lion intelligence officers arrive at League headquarters. They bring data on internal Pride fractures — hardliners versus reformists, old blood versus young ambition. Dave catalogues every name, every schism. The lions came to use him. He will use them first.

choices.text: "The League will consider a limited security cooperation. Subject to full intelligence sharing."

outcome.description: The envoy's mane bristles at 'limited.' But the counter-terms are accepted. Intelligence flows — and with it, Dave sees the cracks in the Lion Sovereignty for the first time. The Pride Council is fracturing. Hardliners push for war. Reformists seek stability. The lions are not offering alliance out of strength. They are offering it out of fear.

choices.text: "The League does not enter alliances with factions that threatened us three arcs ago. Declined."

outcome.description: The envoy departs in cold fury. Dave watches the golden shuttle leave from the observation deck. His intelligence officers are already analysing why the lions came at all. The answer arrives within the hour: internal fractures. The Pride Council is splintering. The lions did not come to ally. They came to survive. Dave files the assessment. Fear is the most reliable intelligence source in the multiverse.

encounters.title: Erratic Contact
encounters.description: Death's ghost ship has been appearing on League sensors with increasing frequency — and decreasing coherence. Three sightings in as many days, each time in a different sector, each time broadcasting fragmented transmissions on frequencies that should not exist. Dave's signals team has been decoding the fragments. The results are disturbing. Death is not attacking. Death is not scheming. Death is raving. The transmissions are a jumble of ancient languages, crystal harmonic frequencies, and what sounds terrifyingly like prayer.

choices.text: "Plot an intercept course. If Death is compromised, this is our best chance to neutralise the threat."

outcome.description: Dave's patrol finds the ghost ship drifting near a dead crystal deposit, its hull pulsing with light that has no source. The ship does not flee. It does not fight. Death's voice whispers across the comms: 'They are waking, Commander. The old ones beneath the crystal. They are waking and they are hungry.' Dave records every word. His analysts will call it madness. Dave is not so sure.

choices.text: "Maintain surveillance distance. Do not engage. Record everything."

outcome.description: Dave's intelligence drones shadow the ghost ship for seventy-two hours. The data is voluminous and deeply unsettling. Death's vessel visits three dead crystal deposits in sequence, performing what can only be described as rituals. The crystal harmonic frequencies spike during each visit. Dave reviews the data alone in his quarters. Something is using Death. Or Death is trying to communicate with something. Neither option is comforting.

choices.text: "Broadcast Death's transmissions to all faction intelligence services. This is a multiverse-level threat."

outcome.description: Dave shares the intelligence openly — an act so uncharacteristic that half the factions assume it is a trick. The fairies respond with alarm; the wolves with contempt; the lions with suspicious silence. But Aristotle's Corsairs transmit a single word in reply: 'Confirmed.' The cat has seen it too. Dave stares at that one word for a long time. If the pirate and the soldier agree, the threat is real.

encounters.title: The Undercurrent Decision
encounters.description: Dave stands in the war room, the ancient chart pinned beside the fairy resonance data beside the lion intelligence beside Death's mad transmissions. Four data streams, one conclusion: the crystal network is not a resource. It is a system. And that system is destabilising. His officers wait. The League High Command has sent three urgent dispatches demanding a strategic recommendation. Dave ignores them all. He is thinking. When Dave thinks, the multiverse waits.

choices.text: "Divert fleet resources to deep crystal research. We need to understand what we are dealing with before we act."

outcome.description: Dave reassigns three cruisers to escort a League science expedition into the deepest crystal deposits. It weakens the blockade. It infuriates High Command. But Dave has read the data, and the data says the crystals are not fuel. They are something else entirely. Understanding that something is now the primary objective. Dave does not explain this to anyone. They will understand when the results arrive.

choices.text: "Reinforce all League positions. Whatever is coming, we face it from a position of strength."

outcome.description: Dave orders a full military consolidation. Patrols double. Supply lines harden. Every League outpost receives reinforcements. It is expensive, exhausting, and exactly what the League does best. High Command is satisfied. Dave is not. Fortification is not understanding. But understanding without survival is academic. He chooses survival first.

choices.text: "Share intelligence selectively. Keep every faction dependent on the League for answers."

outcome.description: Dave parcels out the intelligence like rations — enough to keep each faction engaged, never enough to make them independent. The fairies receive crystal data. The lions receive threat assessments. Even Aristotle receives a fragment, delivered through three intermediaries. Dave sits at the centre of a web of controlled information. It is not honest. It is not clean. But it keeps the League indispensable, and indispensable is the next best thing to invincible.
